family.no_headline: The atlas found no headline statement in this manuscript’s TeX source.
family.lean_scope_heading: What the Lean statements cover, in OpenAI’s words
family.lean_scope_source: From the release’s Lean notes for this result
family.no_lean: No Lean statement accompanies this result in the release.
family.rests_intro: Manuscripts in the collection that this result’s manuscripts cite.
family.rests_none: Its manuscripts cite no other manuscript in the collection.
family.cited_intro: Manuscripts in the collection that cite this result’s manuscripts.
family.cited_none: No other manuscript in the collection cites it.
family.builds_intro: Outside works the manuscripts cite, with where in each manuscript the citation appears.
family.builds_none: The atlas found no outside citations in this manuscript’s sources.
family.superseded: This is an earlier edition. The current edition is {link}.
family.explain_open: This is an open exposition problem. Write an explanation that a mathematician outside the area can follow: what is proved, why it matters and how the argument goes. Claim it first, so two people do not write the same one.
family.xref_title: A cross-reference to {label} in the paper
family.reasoning_summary: OpenAI released an abridged summary of the model's reasoning for this result:
family.formulations_intro: How OpenAI's Lean library states this result's claims as Lean propositions, in the project's Model.lean. Comparator checks only the statements above; the formulations here are stated in the library and are listed so a reader can compare them with the paper.
family.formulations_more: {n} more formulations are in the same file.
family.formulations_theorems: The project also contains {n} theorems named after the manuscript's claims.

statement.sorry_note: A Comparator challenge file states the theorem and leaves its proof as `sorry` on purpose. OpenAI’s proof is in the solution module listed here, and Comparator is the tool that checks that proof against this statement.
statement.sorry_note_axiom: A Comparator challenge file states the theorem and leaves its proof open. This file writes `axiom mainStatement` where others write `sorry`; OpenAI’s solution module proves `main` directly, and Comparator is the tool that checks that proof against this statement.
statement.main_yes: OpenAI lists this as a main result in its Lean catalogue.
statement.main_no: OpenAI’s Lean catalogue does not list this as a main result; the release’s Lean notes for result {id} link it.
statement.permitted_axioms_note: Comparator accepts a proof only if it uses no axioms beyond these.
statement.lines: Lines of Lean, without comments or blank lines
statement.vocab_intro: Everything this file defines for itself. Comparator certifies a proof against exactly this file, so each item is something a reader must check means what the paper means.
statement.vocab_none: This file introduces no definitions of its own: its statement uses Mathlib vocabulary alone.
statement.axiom_heading: A note on how this file states its claim
statement.axiom_note: Line {line} of this statement file writes `axiom mainStatement : MainClaim` where other statement files write `sorry`. It stands in for the proof on the statement side only. OpenAI’s solution proves `main` directly, in {solution_link}. A Comparator replay confirms which axioms that proof uses; the permitted ones are {axioms}.
statement.scope_heading: What the Lean statement covers, in OpenAI’s words
statement.scope_source: From the release’s Lean notes for result {id}
statement.paper_heading: The paper and the Lean statement side by side
statement.paper_intro: Left: the headline statements of the accompanying paper, typeset from its TeX source. Right: the lines of the Lean file that state the theorem.
statement.file_intro: {lines} lines, exactly as in the release at the pinned commit.
statement.card_intro: A card for sharing. It pairs the paper’s statement with the Lean statement; the full file and its vocabulary are below.
statement.card_pairing: The atlas pairs each Lean file with the headline statement of its paper whose words overlap most with the Lean scope note. Every headline statement is shown below.
statement.card_continues: The statement continues in the paper.
statement.checks_none: No reader has filed a check of this statement yet.
statement.replays_none: No independent Comparator replay has been shared yet.
statement.holes_intro: Comparator checks only the name and type of each definition listed here. The body a proof is checked against is the definition in OpenAI’s library, so a reader must read it there as well as in this file.
statement.hole_item: Comparator checks the name and type of `{name}`; its definition is in OpenAI’s library at {link}.
statement.hole_item_nolink: Comparator checks the name and type of `{name}`; its definition is in OpenAI’s library, in the modules that `{module}` imports.
statement.card_holes_one: Comparator checks only the name and type of `{name}`; its definition is in OpenAI’s library.
statement.card_holes_many: Comparator checks only the name and type of {n} definitions, among them `{name}`; their definitions are in OpenAI’s library.
statement.coverage_source: OpenAI’s Lean note for this result

statement.coverage_provenance: Classified from OpenAI’s note by an AI agent; no person has reviewed it yet.
statement.replay_none: No independent Comparator replay is recorded yet. The configuration is OpenAI's.
statement.replay_some: {n} independent Comparator replay receipts are recorded below.
statement.comparator_box_does: When Comparator is run and accepts, OpenAI's proof proves exactly the theorem in this file, with exactly the definitions in this file, using only the permitted axioms, and the Lean kernel accepts every step.

explain.title: Explain a result
explain.lede: Every numbered result in the release is an open exposition problem until someone writes it up for readers outside its area. {open} of {families} are open.
explain.how: Choose one, claim it with the button so others can see it is taken, then write. The contributing guide says what a good explanation contains.

numbers.title: Numbers
numbers.lede: Every number on this site, what it counts and how it is computed. All are read from the release at commit {commit_short}.
numbers.upstream_intro: The release states some figures of its own. They are quoted here with their source, beside the atlas’s nearest count, because the two often measure different things.
numbers.upstream_formalised_atlas: The atlas’s nearest count is {n} current manuscripts with an accompanying Lean statement: manuscripts that a result’s Lean notes list as accompanying papers, whatever part of the paper the Lean statement covers. The two figures count different things, so they differ.
numbers.upstream_catalogue_atlas: The atlas counts {manuscripts} current manuscripts in {families} numbered results.
numbers.upstream_problems_atlas: The atlas does not count problems posed; the release does not list them.
numbers.envs_intro: Theorem-like environments in the TeX sources of the {manuscripts} current manuscripts, by kind.
numbers.withdrawn_intro: The release withdrew {n} manuscripts. Their notices are quoted in full.
numbers.changelog_source: Quoted from the release’s history file

families.label: numbered results
families.definition: The numbered results of the release, each with one or more manuscripts. Some numbers in the sequence are unused.
families.how: Counted from the release’s overview.tex, which lists every result under its discipline, cross-checked against CONTENTS.md.

disciplines.label: disciplines
disciplines.definition: The subject headings under which the release’s overview groups its results.
disciplines.how: Counted from the section headings of overview.tex.

manuscripts_current.label: current manuscripts
manuscripts_current.definition: Manuscripts listed under a result in the release’s overview or contents list, in their current edition.
manuscripts_current.how: Every folder under preprints/ named by a result, excluding withdrawn manuscripts and earlier editions that a newer README replaces.

manuscripts_withdrawn.label: withdrawn manuscripts
manuscripts_withdrawn.definition: Manuscripts whose README carries a withdrawal notice.
manuscripts_withdrawn.how: Counted from the withdrawal notices in each preprint’s README.

manuscripts_previous_editions.label: earlier editions
manuscripts_previous_editions.definition: Manuscript folders that a newer edition lists as its previous version.
manuscripts_previous_editions.how: Counted from the previous-version links in each current README.

statements_lean.label: Lean statements
statements_lean.definition: Comparator challenge files: Lean files that state one theorem each, for Comparator to check a proof against.

statements_lean_main_results.label: Lean statements OpenAI lists as main results
statements_lean_main_results.definition: Comparator challenge files that OpenAI’s lean/formalization.yaml names in its main-results list. The release’s Lean notes link the other challenge files; formalization.yaml does not name them.
statements_lean_main_results.how: Challenge files named by a main-result entry in lean/formalization.yaml.

main_result_declarations.label: main-result declarations
main_result_declarations.definition: Entries in the main-results list of the release’s formalisation record; one challenge file can carry several.
main_result_declarations.how: Counted from the main-results list in lean/formalization.yaml.

families_with_lean.label: results with a Lean statement
families_with_lean.definition: Results whose Lean notes (lean/docs/NNN.md) link at least one Comparator challenge file.
families_with_lean.how: Counted from the statement rows of each result’s Lean notes.

manuscripts_with_lean.label: manuscripts with an accompanying Lean statement
manuscripts_with_lean.how: Current manuscripts named as accompanying papers in a result’s Lean notes, where those notes link at least one challenge file.

lean_statements_pure_mathlib.label: Lean statements in Mathlib vocabulary alone
lean_statements_pure_mathlib.how: Challenge files whose imports are all Mathlib and which declare no definition, structure, instance, notation or axiom of their own.

lean_statements_with_custom_vocabulary.label: Lean statements with vocabulary of their own
lean_statements_with_custom_vocabulary.definition: Comparator challenge files that introduce at least one definition, structure, instance, notation or axiom.
lean_statements_with_custom_vocabulary.how: Challenge files with a vocabulary count of one or more.

lean_statements_importing_non_mathlib.label: Lean statements importing from outside Mathlib
lean_statements_importing_non_mathlib.definition: Comparator challenge files with an import outside Mathlib.
lean_statements_importing_non_mathlib.how: Read from the import lines of each challenge file.

lean_statements_declaring_axioms.label: Lean statement files declaring an axiom
lean_statements_declaring_axioms.definition: Comparator challenge files with an axiom declaration of their own.
lean_statements_declaring_axioms.how: Read from the declarations of each challenge file.

lean_vocabulary_total.label: definitions to check across all Lean statements
lean_vocabulary_total.how: The vocabulary counts of all challenge files, added up. A definition repeated in two files counts twice.

lean_vocabulary_median.label: median definitions to check per Lean statement
lean_vocabulary_median.how: The middle value of the vocabulary counts of all challenge files.

lean_vocabulary_max.label: definitions to check in the largest Lean statement
lean_vocabulary_max.how: The largest vocabulary count of any challenge file.

internal_citation_edges.label: citations between manuscripts in the collection
internal_citation_edges.how: Read from each manuscript’s bibliography: entries linking to an openai/math preprint or keyed OAI:, once per pair.

manuscripts_citing_collection.label: manuscripts that cite another in the collection
manuscripts_citing_collection.definition: Current manuscripts with at least one citation to another manuscript in the collection.
manuscripts_citing_collection.how: Current manuscripts with one or more internal citations.

manuscripts_citing_unformalised_collecti.label: manuscripts citing a manuscript with no accompanying Lean statement
manuscripts_citing_unformalised_collecti.definition: Current manuscripts that cite at least one manuscript in the collection which has no accompanying Lean statement.
manuscripts_citing_unformalised_collecti.how: Current manuscripts with an internal citation whose target is not named in any result’s Lean notes.

external_works_cited.label: outside works cited
external_works_cited.how: Every bibliography entry cited in a current manuscript’s text that does not point into the collection, merged across manuscripts by DOI, then arXiv identifier, then normalised title.

external_citations.label: citations of outside works
external_citations.definition: Bibliography entries cited in the text of current manuscripts that point outside the collection, counted once per manuscript and entry.
external_citations.how: Counted from each manuscript’s cited bibliography entries.

builds_on.title: The work this release builds on
builds_on.lede: The manuscripts in the release cite {works} distinct works outside the collection, {citations} citations in all. These are the {n} works the most manuscripts cite, with every manuscript that cites each one.
builds_on.credit: Each is the work of mathematicians whose results the collection uses directly.
builds_on.how: Works are matched by DOI, then arXiv identifier, then normalised title. Each manuscript counts once per work.

rests_on.title: What the release rests on
rests_on.lede: {edges} citations run between manuscripts inside the collection. These are the {n} manuscripts that the most other current manuscripts cite.
rests_on.cited_by: Cited by {n} manuscripts in the collection
rests_on.how: A citation counts when a manuscript’s bibliography points to another manuscript in the collection, once per citing and cited manuscript.

about.title: About the atlas
about.what: The OpenAI Math Atlas is a reader’s guide to the mathematics OpenAI released on {release_date} in the repository openai/math. It sets out each of the {families} numbered results with the manuscripts that present it, the statements those manuscripts make, the Lean statements that accompany {families_with_lean} of the results, and the citations that tie the collection to itself and to the literature.
about.how: A script reads a pinned checkout of the release (commit {commit_short}) and extracts the contents list, every manuscript’s TeX sources and bibliography, every Comparator challenge file and the Lean notes. A second script turns that into these static pages. Every number is computed from the release; none is typed by hand.
about.independence: The atlas is an independent project. It is not affiliated with or endorsed by OpenAI. It describes what is in the release and what has been checked, and quotes OpenAI’s own words where it describes the results.
about.licence: The release is published by OpenAI under the Apache License 2.0. Descriptions, abstracts, statements, Lean files and notes quoted on these pages come from it unchanged at the pinned commit, and each is attributed where it appears.
about.cite: Cite a page by its address and the pinned commit it describes.
about.author: {author} builds and maintains the atlas. His own work on Erdős problems, with its Lean proofs, is at Plectis.
about.made: Will Cook built the atlas with AI coding agents (Anthropic's Claude) working under his direction. Every number is computed by the scripts in the repository from OpenAI's files at the pinned commit, and the scripts are the source of truth. Classifications made by an AI agent, such as what each Lean statement covers, are labelled as such and wait for a person to review them. Verdicts on the site come only from named people.
about.not: The atlas is not peer review, not an endorsement of any result, and not affiliated with OpenAI. It records what the release contains, what has been checked and by whom, and what is still open.
about.disclosed_heading: What the release's README says about how it was made
about.disclosed_intro: AGMAI's guidance asks labs to disclose the model, prompts, compute and time, and how many comparable problems were tried. OpenAI's README says, in its own words:
about.disclosed_traces: Abridged reasoning summaries for {n} results, linked from those results' pages here.
about.disclosed_not: The README does not list the prompts, the compute for each result, or which of the problems posed were not solved.
about.related_intro: Other places where people are examining AI-generated mathematics.

community.title: Everyone working on this release
community.lede: {efforts} public efforts by {people} people have indexed, checked, replayed, explained or built on OpenAI’s release. {findings} of their findings attach to specific results, and each appears on that result’s page with its author’s name.
community.lede_empty: Public work by other people on this release is being gathered here, each piece credited and linked.
community.credit: The atlas exists alongside this work and draws on it. Findings are cited with their authors and links; code and text are reused only where the author’s licence allows it, and otherwise linked.
community.how: Each entry is a public project, paper, post or organisation, described in the atlas’s words with a link to the original. Listing someone’s work does not mean they endorse the atlas.
